Open Source Ai
docs.text:
A curated catalog of open-source and source-available projects for building AI agents and LLM apps, maintained by CodesbyFebin. This repository contains metadata, comparisons and recipes – not upstream source code. Each project is owned and licensed by its own maintainers.

70 projects · 14 categories · evidence refreshed weekly (freshness report)

  • 🔎 Search & filter the catalog
  • 🧪 Recipes – composed stacks with honest test status
  • 📏 Selection criteria

  • Declared licence is curated by humans in catalog/projects.yaml; needs review entries list a reason on their project page.
  • Flags: archived (upstream archived, kept and labelled), moved (canonical URL changed), licence review, lookup: … (last request failed – previous evidence kept, treat as possibly stale).

docs.title: Selection Criteria
docs.text:
A project is included when it:

  1. Has a licence file. OSI-approved licences are shown as declared SPDX identifiers. Custom, multiple, source-available or undetected licences are marked needs review – read the upstream terms before use; inclusion does not mean the project is freely reusable.
  2. Is maintained or widely used. Activity is recorded weekly in the freshness report; archived projects stay listed and are flagged rather than silently removed.
  3. Is self-hostable or usable as a library without a mandatory vendor account.
  4. Fits a category of the AI agent / LLM stack.

What is what on this site:

  • Catalog data (catalog/projects.yaml): curated descriptions, categories, deployment, hardware, declared licence – edited by humans via pull request.
  • Collected evidence (catalog/evidence/): facts from the GitHub API with source URL and retrieval time.
  • Editorial ("Highlight" columns, recipes choice): opinion, labelled as such.
  • Upstream claims: anything in a project's own README; not verified here.
  • Test results: only recipes marked tested, with environment and date.

Stars and popularity are not used as a proxy for quality or security.

docs.title: How-to: Connect Any Tool to a Gateway
docs.text:
Every stack here speaks the OpenAI API. Set: 

export OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000/v1
export OPENAI_API_KEY=<your gateway key>
In UIs (Open WebUI, Dify, Flowise) add a custom OpenAI-compatible provider with the same URL.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Open Source Ai is a catalog: it links to upstream projects instead of bundling them.

  1. Find projects – use Search & Filter or browse a category in the navigation.
  2. Check fit – each project's detail section lists deployment, hardware, licence (with evidence link) and activity.
  3. Install from upstream – follow the project's linked setup docs, or clone only what you need: 
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ollama/ollama
  4. Compose a stack – start from a recipe: 
    git clone https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/Open-Source-Ai
cd Open-Source-Ai/recipes/local-chat && docker compose up -d

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
Recipes compose a few catalogued projects into a working stack. Each states exactly what was tested, where and when. The catalog does not operate or support upstream software.

docs.title: Agent with persistent memory and evaluation – Open Source Ai recipe
docs.text:
Test status: unverified

Not yet run end-to-end. Missing evidence: a successful run of agent.py with Mem0's Ollama provider and a passing promptfoo eval. Treat the commands as a starting point.

docs.title: Agent with persistent memory and evaluation: Ollama + Mem0 + Qdrant + promptfoo
docs.text: Data flow: agent.py remember → Mem0 → Ollama embeddings → Qdrant · agent.py ask → Mem0 search (Qdrant) → Ollama chat with retrieved facts · promptfoo runs agent.py ask and asserts on the answers.

docs.title: Pinned versions
docs.text: Component Version Ollama ollama/ollama:0.40.6 Qdrant qdrant/qdrant:v1.19.2 Mem0 mem0ai==2.2.1 (see requirements.txt) promptfoo promptfoo@0.124.1 Models qwen2.5:1.5b (~1 GB), nomic-embed-text:v1.5 (~0.3 GB)

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Docker 24+ with Compose v2, Python 3.10+, Node.js 18+
  • 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, ~6 GB disk; no GPU needed. Cold start ~3–5 minutes (image + model pulls).

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
cd Open-Source-Ai/recipes/agent-memory-eval
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
./smoke.sh          # full end-to-end test (cleans up on exit; KEEP=1 to keep containers)

Or step by step:

docker compose up -d && docker compose wait model-pull
python agent.py remember "My favourite programming language is Rust."
docker compose restart qdrant              # memory survives the restart
python agent.py recall "favourite language"
python agent.py ask "Which programming language does the user prefer?"
npx promptfoo@0.124.1 eval

remember stores facts verbatim (infer=False) so the test is deterministic; set INFER=1 to let the LLM extract facts (less reliable with small models).

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text: docker compose down -v && rm -rf .venv

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Tests memory storage, persistence across a Qdrant restart and a new process, and that answers use stored facts. Does not test Mem0's LLM-based fact extraction, multi-user isolation or tool use.
  • Small models can phrase answers unexpectedly; assertions only check for the key word.

docs.title: Local private chat (model + gateway + chat UI) – Open Source Ai recipe
docs.text:
Test status: tested

CI job recipe-local-chat runs recipes/local-chat/smoke.sh on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest (4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, no GPU) on every push and PR. It validates the compose file, pulls qwen2.5:0.5b, asks the gateway 17+25 and asserts the reply contains 42 with non-zero completion tokens, checks ollama ps shows the model loaded and Ollama's log shows the chat request, and checks the Open WebUI health endpoint. Pinned: Ollama 0.40.6, LiteLLM v1.106.1, Open WebUI v0.12.3. Not tested: GPUs, larger models, the browser chat flow in Open WebUI.

docs.title: Local private chat: Ollama + LiteLLM + Open WebUI
docs.text: Data flow: browser → Open WebUI (:3000) → LiteLLM gateway (:4000, OpenAI-compatible) → Ollama (:11434) → local model. Nothing leaves your machine after the first image/model download.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Minimum (tested) For bigger models CPU / RAM 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM 16 GB+ RAM, NVIDIA GPU or Apple Silicon Disk ~8 GB (images + 0.4 GB model) 25 GB+ Software Docker 24+ with Compose v2 – Network Internet for first pull only –

No accounts or paid API keys are needed.

docs.title: Pinned versions
docs.text:
Component Version Ollama ollama/ollama:0.40.6 LiteLLM ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.106.1 Open WebUI ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:v0.12.3 Model qwen2.5:0.5b (~0.4 GB)

Typical cold start on a 4-vCPU CI runner: about 2 minutes (image pulls dominate).

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/CodesbyFebin/Open-Source-Ai
cd Open-Source-Ai/recipes/local-chat
export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-$(openssl rand -hex 12)   # never commit real keys
docker compose up -d
docker compose wait model-pull

Environment variables: LITELLM_MASTER_KEY (gateway key, default is a placeholder), MODEL (Ollama model, default qwen2.5:0.5b; also change litellm-config.yaml).

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
./smoke.sh     # same test CI runs; asks 17+25 and checks the model answers 42,
               # token usage is reported, and Ollama's own log shows the request
# or manually
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -d '{"model":"local-llama","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi"}]}'

Open http://localhost:3000, create the first (admin) account and pick local-llama.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
docker compose down        # keep data
docker compose down -v     # also delete models and chats

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• qwen2.5:0.5b is a tiny model chosen so CI can run on CPU; answers are low quality. Use a 3B–8B model for real use.
  • Ollama model tags are not immutable; the digest actually pulled is printed by ollama list in the CI log.
